concept:
Character concept for a 2D cut-out animation game. Draw ONE original creature: an EMERALD-CRYSTAL WOLF, the SECOND stage of a two-stage Wood evolution line whose first stage is image 6: the emerald-crystal fox cub, in the same view and pose as image 1, crouched low on four legs ready to pounce, on a plain white background. A cute, chunky creature, but an original design that must look clearly DIFFERENT from the figure the silhouette came from; not any existing character.

Image 1 (grey silhouette) and image 2 (the same figure split into numbered regions) show the PUPPET RIG the new creature will be animated on. They tell you where each part and joint is, NOT what the creature looks like: do not trace their outline. Viewer-left and viewer-right mean as seen in the picture.

KEEP FROM THE RIG (the animation moves these parts around these joints):
- the same parts, no more, no fewer, each where its numbered region is: 1 head with face and crystal horns; 2 silver-grey mane; 3 body with crystal back; 4 four legs; 5 two wings of emerald crystal blades; 6 bushy tail with crystal leaves;
- every joint where it is and every part pointing the same way as in image 1; eyes where the old eyes are;
- each part about the size and shape of its region; the whole figure about the same size.

CHANGE (the new look, region by region):
1 head with face and crystal horns: the grown-up crystal wolf head: slate-grey head, a cream muzzle with small fangs, one lemon-yellow eye (one catchlight dot) exactly where the old eye is, a brow angled down, a confident snarl-grin; a slate-grey pointed ear with a cream inside where the green ear is; the two horns become two big curved horns of flat emerald-green crystal with a few darker emerald facet lines, the same places and sweep; no crown, no glow, no flame wisp, no brown.
2 silver-grey mane: a big fluffy silver-grey mane with the same spiky tufts, the tuft tips a lighter silver grey (flat colours, no white, no teal).
3 body with crystal back: a slate-grey body with a cream belly and a row of small flat emerald crystal shards along the back.
4 four legs: slate-grey legs in the same places with cream lower legs and paws and short dark-grey claws; the two orange leaves on the haunch become two flat emerald crystal shards; no orange, no yellow spots, no brown stripes.
5 two wings of emerald crystal blades: the wings become fans of long flat emerald-green crystal blades like ribbons, each blade with a darker emerald facet line down the middle, fanned out the same way; no leaf veins, no glow, no sparkle.
6 bushy tail with crystal leaves: a big bushy slate-grey tail with a cream tip, carrying a cluster of flat emerald crystal leaves near the tip; no white, no teal.

ATTITUDE: a fierce but cute crystal wolf about to pounce: brow angled down, a confident snarl-grin with small fangs; cute, never scary, never a cheerful mascot.

{RENDER}
{DESIGN}
The style sheet is image 3; the hand-drawn map is image 4. Image 5 is an approved character of this game: copy its ink line weight and its pencil and crayon texture, not its design; it has a few white shine spots and some darker shading: do NOT copy those. Image 6 is the approved first stage of this creature: keep its colours, face and drawing style; this stage is the same creature grown up.

COLOURS: slate-grey fur, a cream belly and muzzle, a silver-grey mane, flat emerald-green crystal horns, wing blades and shards with a few darker emerald facet lines (no sparkle), lemon-yellow eyes. Few colours.

AVOID: a green body, orange ears, red eyes, white fur, brown horns, leaves on a stem, a red berry, a glowing magic circle on the ground, a gold crown, glowing green flame wisps, sparkles, crystal shine, text, labels, numbers, the region colours, frames, background scenery, a second view, shading, shadows, white highlights, glossy shine, glow, gradients.
